summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of kidney transplant, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and coronary artery disease, was admitted for new-onset shortness of breath characterized by difficulty taking deep breaths and fatigue, without chest pain or fever. Initial concern for heart failure or pulmonary embolism was raised due to elevated BNP and d-dimer, but troponin was normal and chest X-ray showed only minimal pulmonary congestion without frank edema. His symptoms were attributed to fluid overload, likely due to holding his home diuretic (torsemide) after a recent hospitalization for gout. He received IV furosemide with significant improvement in breathing. Kidney function, though initially elevated, was deemed stable near his baseline by the transplant team, supported by a normal renal ultrasound with only a new small cyst noted. He was discharged on his home diuretic and medications with instructions to follow up for ongoing management.
problems: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease with stage 1 through stage 4 chronic kidney disease, or unspecified chronic kidney disease
Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris
Benign prostatic hyperplasia without lower urinary tract symptoms
